description: Forestry explores forests as living systems and working landscapes: identifying trees, wood and growth rings, what forests give us, sustainable management, field visits with foresters, tree hazards, forest threats, and wildfire.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. Excerpts listed the topics in order with approximate numbering; confirm the numbering against the official page. The 2026 update revised the managed-forest and logging-visit items.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Identifying trees
requirements.summary: Identifying local trees, shrubs and vines and their features, habitats and uses.

requirements.title: Wood or growth rings
requirements.summary: One option: collecting wood samples, or studying growth rings in stumps, logs or cores.

requirements.title: Benefits of forests
requirements.summary: How forests contribute to the economy, recreation, soil, water, air and wildlife.

requirements.title: Forest management
requirements.summary: Multiple-use and sustainable management and common cutting systems.

requirements.title: Field visits
requirements.summary: Visiting a managed forest and a logging or mill operation, and fire prevention.

requirements.title: Tree hazards
requirements.summary: An inventory of hazardous trees, or reviewing a professional hazard report.

requirements.title: Forest threats and wildfire
requirements.summary: Threats such as wildfire, insects and overgrazing, and what to do if you find a forest fire.
